title: Short Stuff: Schmidt Stinging Pain Index
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Schmidt Sting Pain Index, a scale created by entomologist Justin O. Schmidt that rates the pain of insect stings. The hosts describe how Schmidt developed the index (published in 1984 while at the University of Georgia, later at the University of Arizona), his many stings, and his vivid descriptions of pain for sweat bees, fire ants, bald-faced hornets, yellow jackets, red harvest ants, paper wasps, tarantula hawk wasps, and bullet ants. Josh shares a personal story about being stung eleven times by yellow jackets while camping, and Chuck mentions his daughter's wasp sting.

segments.title: Opening and introduction to Justin Schmidt
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Short Stuff episode, filling in for Dave, and introduces entomologist Justin O. Schmidt and his sting pain index. The hosts discuss the origin of the index, Schmidt's work at the University of Georgia and later the University of Arizona, and how he cataloged stings from many species.

segments.title: Sweat bees, fire ants and bald-faced hornets
segments.summary: The hosts go through the lower end of the scale. Sweat bees rate a one and feel like a tiny spark singeing a hair. Fire ants are also a one, described as a sharp, mildly alarming sting. Bald-faced hornets rate a two, described as rich, hearty and slightly crunchy.

segments.title: Yellow jackets and Josh's camping stings
segments.summary: Yellow jackets rate a two and are described as hot and smoky. Josh recounts being stung eleven times in the face and neck by yellow jackets from a ground nest while camping, with one deeply embedded stinger lasting longer than ten minutes.

segments.title: Red harvest ants and paper wasps
segments.summary: Red harvest ants rate a three and are described as bold and unrelenting, lasting for hours. The hosts then discuss paper wasps, rated 3.0, which Chuck's daughter was stung by. The sting lasted about fifteen minutes.

segments.title: Tarantula hawk wasp and bullet ant
segments.summary: Chuck's daughter found a purple and orange tarantula wasp, which has one of the most painful stings, rated four plus. The bullet ant, a Central and South American ant, is also rated at the top of the scale, with its pain described as twelve hours of intense, brilliant pain. The hosts mention people who deliberately get stung to test the index.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh closes the episode, advising listeners to steer clear of stinging insects and to check the Schmidt index if they are stung. Credit to iHeartRadio is given.
